q: Continuing the scenario, what is the correct total DAEDS RPF Architect Reyes should charge for the 15-unit project?
n: 1st unit = 10% x PHP 1,200,000 = PHP 120,000. Units 2–10 (9 additional, 50%) = 50% x PHP 120,000 x 9 = PHP 540,000, giving PHP 660,000 for 10 units. Units 11–15 (5 additional, 40%) = 40% x PHP 120,000 x 5 = PHP 240,000. Total = PHP 660,000 + PHP 240,000 = PHP 900,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: Architect Reyes is engaged by a developer to design a 15-unit row-house project on one consolidated lot, using a single set of plans/design, specifications and related documents for all units. PCC is PHP 1,200,000.00 per unit.

q: Continuing the scenario, what is the DAEDS RPF contributed by units 2 through 10 (the 2–10 bracket, 9 additional units)?
n: Units 2–10 add 50% of the first-unit RPF per additional unit: 50% x PHP 300,000 x 9 additional units = PHP 1,350,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged for a housing project consisting of one house plan implemented 25 times on a single site (25 residential units, one set of plans), with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 3,000,000.00 per unit.

q: For unit 51 and above of a Group VII housing project, the DAEDS fee is computed as:
o: Fee for 30 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 9% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 25% of RPF for each additional unit
n: For the 51st unit and above, the DAEDS fee is the fee already computed for 50 units, plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit beyond the 50th — the lowest marginal rate in the DAEDS scale.

q: Which issuance of the Board/Institute establishes the Building Type Group classifications (Groups I through X, including Group VII) and their corresponding Recommended Professional Fee scales referenced in this reviewer?
o: SPP Document 202 (Schedule of Recommended Professional Fees for Regular Design Services)
The Code of Ethical Conduct for Architects
n: The Building Type Group classifications (Group VII being Housing Projects) and their fee scales are found in SPP (Standard/Standardized Professional Practice) Document 202, which governs Regular Design Services professional fees, at Sec. 6.3.7.

q: What is the TOTAL DADS RPF for the same 25-unit housing project?
n: 1st unit (DADS) = 6% x PHP 3,000,000 = PHP 180,000. Units 2–10 (9 additional units) add 30% of RPF each: 30% x PHP 180,000 x 9 = PHP 486,000, giving PHP 666,000 for 10 units. Units 11–25 (15 additional units, 11–30 bracket) add 24% of RPF each: 24% x PHP 180,000 x 15 = PHP 648,000. Total = PHP 666,000 + PHP 648,000 = PHP 1,314,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged for a housing project consisting of one house plan implemented 25 times on a single site (25 residential units, one set of plans), with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 3,000,000.00 per unit.

q: Under the DADS scale for Group VII, the fee for units 31 to 50 is computed as:
o: Fee for 50 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 30 units plus 25% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 30 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 30 units plus 9% of RPF for each additional unit
n: Under DADS, the 31st to 50th unit bracket is the fee for 30 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit.

q: Which of the following is the essential qualifying condition for a housing project to be charged under the Group VII fee scale?
o: The Architect must be a sole practitioner, not a firm
The project must consist of exactly ten (10) units or more
The units must be built on a single site using one (1) set of plans/design, specifications, and related documents
The units must all be sold to the same buyer
n: Group VII's scale applies only when several residential units are constructed on a single site sharing one set of plans/design, specs and related documents — not merely when a project has many units.

q: What is the TOTAL DADS RPF for the same 40-unit project?
n: 1st unit (DADS) = 6% x PHP 1,000,000 = PHP 60,000. Units 2–10 (9 additional, 30% each) = 30% x PHP 60,000 x 9 = PHP 162,000, giving PHP 222,000 for 10 units. Units 11–30 (20 additional, 24% each) = 24% x PHP 60,000 x 20 = PHP 288,000, giving PHP 510,000 for 30 units. Units 31–40 (10 additional, 15% each) = 15% x PHP 60,000 x 10 = PHP 90,000. Total = PHP 510,000 + PHP 90,000 = PHP 600,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: A housing project of 40 identical units is built on a single site from one set of plans, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 1,000,000.00 per unit.

q: Using the scenario above, what is the DAEDS-based RPF for this 2-unit housing project?
n: 1st unit (DAEDS) = 10% x PHP 800,000 = PHP 80,000. The 2nd unit (within the 2–10 bracket) adds 50% of that RPF: 50% x PHP 80,000 = PHP 40,000. Total = PHP 80,000 + PHP 40,000 = PHP 120,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged to design a small housing project of 2 identical residential units on a single site, using one (1) set of plans/design, specifications and related documents. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is PHP 800,000.00 per unit.

q: For a Group VII housing project, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the first unit under Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS)?
n: Under Group VII, the DAEDS fee for the first unit is 10% of PCC.

q: What is the TOTAL DADS RPF for the same 60-unit project?
n: 1st unit (DADS) = 6% x PHP 1,500,000 = PHP 90,000. Units 2–10 (9 additional, 30%) = PHP 243,000, giving PHP 333,000 for 10 units. Units 11–30 (20 additional, 24%) = PHP 432,000, giving PHP 765,000 for 30 units. Units 31–50 (20 additional, 15%) = PHP 270,000, giving PHP 1,035,000 for 50 units. Units 51–60 (10 additional, 9%) = 9% x PHP 90,000 x 10 = PHP 81,000. Total = PHP 1,035,000 + PHP 81,000 = PHP 1,116,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: A large housing project of 60 identical units is built on a single site from one set of plans, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 1,500,000.00 per unit.

q: Using the same scenario, what is the total DADS RPF for this 5-unit project?
n: 1st unit (DADS) = 6% x PHP 2,000,000 = PHP 120,000. Units 2–5 (4 additional units) add 30% of RPF each: 30% x PHP 120,000 x 4 = PHP 144,000. Total = PHP 120,000 + PHP 144,000 = PHP 264,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect designs a 5-unit housing project (single site, one set of plans) with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 2,000,000.00 per unit.

q: For units 11 to 30 of a Group VII housing project, the DAEDS fee is computed as:
o: Fee for 10 units plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 10 units plus 50% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for one unit plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 10 units plus 24% of RPF for each additional unit
n: For the 11th to 30th unit bracket, the DAEDS fee is the fee already computed for 10 units, plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit beyond the 10th.

q: A different developer asks Architect Cruz to design a 30-unit housing project on a single site, but insists that each of the 30 units be individually and distinctly designed with its own separate architectural plans (no plan is repeated). How should Architect Cruz classify and charge this engagement?
o: As a Group VII Housing Project, using the 30-unit DAEDS/DADS bracket fee

Not as a Group VII Housing Project, since Group VII presupposes one set of plans/design used across the units; 30 individually and distinctly designed units would instead be charged individually (e.g., under the applicable building-type group for each design, or under Group VI if the repetitive-building criteria are met)
As a Group VII Housing Project, but only charging for the first unit since the rest are 'additional units'
As a Group VI project, because there are more than ten buildings
n: Group VII's tiered discount scale is premised on several units sharing one set of plans/design, specifications and related documents. Where every unit is individually and distinctly designed, that premise is absent, so the project would not be charged under the Group VII bracket scale but rather assessed on its own basis (e.g., each unit under its applicable building-type classification).

q: Continuing the scenario, what is the DAEDS RPF contributed by units 11 through 25 (the 11–30 bracket, 15 additional units)?
n: Units 11–25 fall in the 11–30 bracket, which adds 40% of the first-unit RPF per additional unit: 40% x PHP 300,000 x 15 additional units = PHP 1,800,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged for a housing project consisting of one house plan implemented 25 times on a single site (25 residential units, one set of plans), with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 3,000,000.00 per unit.

q: Under the DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services) scale for Group VII, what percentage of RPF is charged for each additional unit within the 2–10 unit bracket?
o: 30% of RPF for each additional unit
24% of RPF for each additional unit
50% of RPF for each additional unit
40% of RPF for each additional unit
n: Under DADS, units 2 to 10 add 30% of RPF per additional unit (compared to DAEDS's 50%).

q: What is the practical rationale behind giving Group VII housing projects a declining marginal fee percentage per additional unit (rather than charging 100% of RPF for every unit)?
o: Because the National Building Code caps total professional fees for any project at a fixed amount
To penalize developers for building affordable housing

Because reusing one set of plans/design across multiple repetitive units on the same site requires proportionately less additional design effort per unit as more units are added, so the fee scale reflects that economy of scale while still compensating the Architect for each unit built
Because only the first and last units in a housing project actually get built to the approved plans
n: The graduated, declining percentages (e.g., DAEDS 50%→40%→25%→15%) recognize that once the Architect has produced one set of plans/design/specifications, applying it to additional identical units involves less incremental design work than the original unit, while still fairly compensating the Architect on a per-unit basis as the project scales up.

q: Using the scenario above, what is the DAEDS RPF for the first 30 units of this project (i.e., the cumulative fee through the 31–50 bracket's starting point)?
n: 1st unit = 10% x PHP 1,000,000 = PHP 100,000. Units 2–10 (9 additional units, 50% each) = 50% x PHP 100,000 x 9 = PHP 450,000, giving PHP 550,000 for 10 units. Units 11–30 (20 additional units, 40% each) = 40% x PHP 100,000 x 20 = PHP 800,000. Fee for 30 units = PHP 550,000 + PHP 800,000 = PHP 1,350,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: A housing project of 40 identical units is built on a single site from one set of plans, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 1,000,000.00 per unit.

q: Under the DADS scale for Group VII, the fee for unit 51 and above is computed as:
o: Fee for 30 units plus 9% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 9% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 24% of RPF for each additional unit
n: Under DADS, unit 51 and above is the fee for 50 units plus 9% of RPF for each additional unit — the lowest marginal rate in the DADS scale.

q: A developer asks an Architect to design 20 individual houses on 20 different (non-contiguous) subdivision lots scattered across a city, each with its own separately prepared plan. Does this project qualify for the Group VII (Housing Project) fee scale?
o: No, because Group VII only applies to condominium units, not detached houses
Yes, because there are more than ten residential units involved
No, because Group VII requires the units to be on a single site and use one set of plans/design and specifications — separate sites and separate plans take it outside Group VII
Yes, because all the units are residential in nature
n: Group VII specifically requires (1) a single site and (2) one set of plans/design, specifications and related documents for all units. Scattered sites with individually prepared plans do not meet either condition, so the tiered Group VII scale would not apply.

q: Using the scenario above, what is the DAEDS RPF for the first 50 units of this project?
n: 1st unit = 10% x PHP 1,500,000 = PHP 150,000. Units 2–10 (9 additional, 50%) = 50% x PHP 150,000 x 9 = PHP 675,000, giving PHP 825,000 for 10 units. Units 11–30 (20 additional, 40%) = 40% x PHP 150,000 x 20 = PHP 1,200,000, giving PHP 2,025,000 for 30 units. Units 31–50 (20 additional, 25%) = 25% x PHP 150,000 x 20 = PHP 750,000. Fee for 50 units = PHP 2,025,000 + PHP 750,000 = PHP 2,775,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: A large housing project of 60 identical units is built on a single site from one set of plans, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 1,500,000.00 per unit.

q: Using the same scenario, what is the DADS-based RPF for this 2-unit housing project?
n: 1st unit (DADS) = 6% x PHP 800,000 = PHP 48,000. The 2nd unit adds 30% of that RPF: 30% x PHP 48,000 = PHP 14,400. Total = PHP 48,000 + PHP 14,400 = PHP 62,400.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged to design a small housing project of 2 identical residential units on a single site, using one (1) set of plans/design, specifications and related documents. The Project Construction Cost (PCC) is PHP 800,000.00 per unit.

q: For a Group VII housing project, what is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for the first unit under Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS)?
n: Under Group VII, the DADS fee for the first unit is 6% of PCC (lower than DAEDS's 10%, since DADS excludes the engineering design component).

q: In the scenario above, which bracket of the Group VII fee scale governs the fee for units 11 to 15?
o: The 31–50 bracket (fee for 30 units plus 25% of RPF per additional unit)
The 11–30 bracket (fee for 10 units plus 40% of RPF per additional unit)
The 2–10 bracket (50% of RPF per additional unit)
Group VII does not apply because there are more than 10 units
n: With 15 total units, units 11 through 15 fall within the 11–30 unit bracket, where the DAEDS/DADS fee is the fee already computed for 10 units plus the applicable marginal percentage (40% DAEDS / 24% DADS) of RPF for each unit beyond the 10th. Group VII has no upper unit-count limit — it simply adds further brackets (31–50, 51+) as the count grows.
scenario: SCENARIO: Architect Reyes is engaged by a developer to design a 15-unit row-house project on one consolidated lot, using a single set of plans/design, specifications and related documents for all units. PCC is PHP 1,200,000.00 per unit.

q: Using the scenario above, what is the DAEDS RPF for the first unit alone?
n: The DAEDS fee for the first unit is 10% of PCC: 10% x PHP 3,000,000 = PHP 300,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged for a housing project consisting of one house plan implemented 25 times on a single site (25 residential units, one set of plans), with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 3,000,000.00 per unit.

q: For units 31 to 50 of a Group VII housing project, the DAEDS fee is computed as:
o: Fee for 30 units plus 25% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 30 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 30 units plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 50 units plus 25% of RPF for each additional unit
n: For the 31st to 50th unit bracket, the DAEDS fee is the fee already computed for 30 units, plus 25% of RPF for each additional unit beyond the 30th.

q: An Architect completes the design for a Group VII housing project of 12 units (one set of plans, single site). Midway through construction, the developer decides to add 3 more identical units (bringing the total to 15) using the exact same plans. How should the Architect's additional fee for these 3 units be computed?
o: Free of charge, since the plans have already been paid for
At the full 100% first-unit RPF rate for each of the 3 additional units
As entirely new Group IV or V fees, unrelated to the original 12-unit computation

As additional units within the Group VII bracket scale, continuing the tiered computation from where the 12-unit fee left off (i.e., these 3 additional units still fall in the 11–30 bracket, at 40% of RPF each for DAEDS)
n: Because the added units reuse the same single set of plans on the same site, they remain within the Group VII scope; the fee for the 3 additional units continues the same bracket progression (11–30 bracket at this unit count), rather than being computed as a separate or unrelated fee.

q: What is the TOTAL DAEDS RPF for this 25-unit housing project?
n: Total DAEDS RPF = fee for 1st unit + fee for units 2–10 + fee for units 11–25 = PHP 300,000 + PHP 1,350,000 + PHP 1,800,000 = PHP 3,450,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect is engaged for a housing project consisting of one house plan implemented 25 times on a single site (25 residential units, one set of plans), with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 3,000,000.00 per unit.

q: Under the DADS scale for Group VII, the fee for units 11 to 30 is computed as:
o: Fee for 30 units plus 24% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 10 units plus 15% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 10 units plus 40% of RPF for each additional unit
Fee for 10 units plus 24% of RPF for each additional unit
n: Under DADS, the 11th to 30th unit bracket is the fee for 10 units plus 24% of RPF for each additional unit.

q: Under SPP Document 202, what kind of project falls under Building Type Group VII?
o: A single monumental building of unique design
The repetitive construction of similar but separately-designed buildings on different sites
An alteration, renovation, or expansion of an existing residential building
A Housing Project involving the construction of several residential units on a single site using one (1) set of plans/design, specifications and related documents
n: Group VII covers Housing Projects: several residential units built on a single site, all sharing one set of plans/design, specifications, and related contract documents.

q: Continuing the scenario, what is the TOTAL DAEDS RPF for all 40 units (units 31–40 fall in the 31–50 bracket, at 25% of RPF per additional unit)?
n: Fee for 30 units = PHP 1,350,000. Units 31–40 (10 additional units, 31–50 bracket) add 25% of RPF each: 25% x PHP 100,000 x 10 = PHP 250,000. Total = PHP 1,350,000 + PHP 250,000 = PHP 1,600,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: A housing project of 40 identical units is built on a single site from one set of plans, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 1,000,000.00 per unit.

q: What overall pattern describes the Group VII fee scale as the number of units in a housing project increases (for both DAEDS and DADS)?
o: The fee is a flat percentage of PCC regardless of the number of units

The marginal percentage charged per additional unit decreases with each successive bracket (e.g., DAEDS goes 50% → 40% → 25% → 15%), reflecting economies of scale from reusing the same set of plans across more units
Only the first ten units are charged a fee; all units beyond the 10th are provided free of charge
The marginal percentage charged per additional unit increases with each bracket, rewarding larger projects with a higher fee rate
n: Both the DAEDS (50%→40%→25%→15%) and DADS (30%→24%→15%→9%) scales step down the marginal percentage applied to each additional unit as the project moves into higher unit-count brackets, since re-using one set of plans across more repetitive units involves proportionately less additional design effort per unit.

q: How does Group VII (Housing Projects) differ from Group VI (repetitive construction of similar buildings) under SPP Document 202's Building Type classification?
o: Group VI uses unit-count brackets (1, 2–10, 11–30…), while Group VI uses per-building brackets (1st, 2nd, 3rd…)

Group VI grades fee reduction per successive whole building (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and succeeding) using a single flat percentage scale of the building-type RPF; Group VII grades fee reduction per residential unit using its own DAEDS/DADS percentage-of-PCC base rates and unit-count brackets
Group VI applies only to institutional buildings, while Group VII applies only to commercial buildings
They are identical; Group VII is simply the newer designation for Group VI
n: Group VI (Sec. 6.3.6) reduces fees per successive similar building built from the same unamended drawings (100%/50%/40%/30% of the building type's RPF for the 1st/2nd/3rd/4th-and-succeeding buildings). Group VII (Sec. 6.3.7) instead grades the fee per residential unit within a single housing project, computed from its own DAEDS (10% of PCC) or DADS (6% of PCC) base rate for the first unit, then a declining percentage for each additional unit across brackets (2–10, 11–30, 31–50, 51+).

q: Continuing the scenario, what is the TOTAL DAEDS RPF for all 60 units (units 51–60 fall in the 51-and-above bracket, at 15% of RPF per additional unit)?
n: Fee for 50 units = PHP 2,775,000. Units 51–60 (10 additional units, 51+ bracket) add 15% of RPF each: 15% x PHP 150,000 x 10 = PHP 225,000. Total = PHP 2,775,000 + PHP 225,000 = PHP 3,000,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: A large housing project of 60 identical units is built on a single site from one set of plans, with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 1,500,000.00 per unit.

q: Using the scenario above, what is the total DAEDS RPF for this 5-unit project?
n: 1st unit (DAEDS) = 10% x PHP 2,000,000 = PHP 200,000. Units 2–5 (4 additional units, within the 2–10 bracket) add 50% of RPF each: 50% x PHP 200,000 x 4 = PHP 400,000. Total = PHP 200,000 + PHP 400,000 = PHP 600,000.00.
scenario: SCENARIO: An Architect designs a 5-unit housing project (single site, one set of plans) with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 2,000,000.00 per unit.

q: For units 2 to 10 of a Group VII housing project, how is the additional DAEDS fee per additional unit computed?
o: 50% of the RPF (first-unit fee) for each additional unit
100% of the RPF (first-unit fee) for each additional unit
30% of the RPF (first-unit fee) for each additional unit
40% of the RPF (first-unit fee) for each additional unit
n: For the 2nd to 10th unit bracket, the DAEDS fee is the fee for one unit plus 50% of RPF for each additional unit in that bracket.
